target_customer: Employers, health plans and pharmacy benefit managers that pay for substance use care for members; originally smokers paying directly
problem: People struggling with tobacco, alcohol or opioid use have limited access to affordable, evidence based treatment.
business_model: B2B2C per member or outcomes based contracts with employers and health plans; started as consumer app subscriptions at 4 and 15 dollars per month
product_category: Virtual clinic for substance use management (digital CBT plus medication assisted treatment)

founders.name: Yusuf Sherwani
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a medical doctor. TechCrunch (Feb 2018): the three founders met on the first day of medical school at Imperial College London.

founders.name: Maroof Ahmed
founders.background_notes: Named cofounder and COO by TechCrunch (Feb 2018); not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Sarim Siddiqui
founders.role: Chief Medical Officer (Head of Product in 2018)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as co-founder, CMO and MD.

competitors.name: Pear Therapeutics (reSET)
competitors.what: Prescription digital therapeutic for substance use disorder
competitors.traction_then: reSET was released in November 2018 after FDA clearance, so it was in development at the time of the batch
competitors.funding_then: 50 million dollar Series B in 2018 led by Temasek per search summary of Law360

technical_complexity.rationale: A CBT app with video, audio and diary features is standard mobile engineering; the harder parts were clinical validation and later medication prescribing and care operations.

defensibility.rationale: Clinical evidence, licensed clinicians and payer contracts build over time, but the original app content was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it; Pear Therapeutics' reSET was released in November 2018 and Pelago kept raising through 2024.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (Feb 2018) reports the founders saw smoking harm patients as medical students, cited cessation therapy costs of 2,000 to 4,000 dollars, and an Imperial College study claiming 36 percent of users quit.

branding.name_origin: Pelago is short for archipelago, reflecting the idea that you are not an island; islands drifted from the continent but stay connected, per the company blog (June 2023).
branding.domain_note: Used quitgenius.com until rebrand; pelagohealth.com since.

identity.logo: Not described in the company blog; identity designed by A LINE
identity.visual_style: Pelago yellow with moss green, maroon and tan, serif typeface, slightly askew icons
identity.voice_and_tone: Optimistic, honest, an ally to members

rebrands.why: Old name focused on quitting and tobacco, was hard to pronounce (people said quick genius) and did not fit alcohol or other substance support; stigma reduction goal

branding.community_and_virality: Rebrand covered by Transform Magazine and Creative Boom; no evidence of viral or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Designed rebrand with trade press coverage and a clear rationale, but a B2B health brand with limited public awareness.

pivots.to: Digital clinic for opioid, alcohol and tobacco addiction sold to employers and health plans
pivots.why: TechCrunch headline says the Series A funded expansion into opioid and alcohol treatment

pivots.to: Pelago brand and broader behavioral health platform
pivots.why: Name no longer fit the broader substance use scope

outcome_analysis: Quit Genius began as a 4 dollar per month smoking cessation app from three Imperial College medical graduates, then expanded into a clinic for alcohol and opioid use sold to employers and health plans. It raised an 11 million dollar Series A in 2020, 64 million in 2021 and 58 million in 2024, bringing the reported total to about 151 million dollars, and renamed itself Pelago in 2023. It is active with about 180 staff.
notes: TechCrunch (Mar 2024) states a total of 151 million dollars, which matches the five rounds recorded (0.9 + 1.1 + 11 + 64 + 58 = 135) only partly; about 16 million dollars is unexplained, so a grant or other round may be missing. Series A, Series B and May 2018 seed details come from search result summaries and article URLs, not opened pages except as cited. Pear Therapeutics' 2018 Series B date is not given by the source seen and reSET launched after the batch, so it is included as a near-batch rival. The Feb 2018 TechCrunch article names no competitors. No layoffs, acquisition or IPO news found for 2024 and 2025 in the outcome search.
